Implement the following requested change in the repository.

Monokai style color changes cause contrast degradation

Description

At these lines: https://github.com/pygments/pygments/blob/master/pygments/styles/monokai.py#L31-L112

Several color values in the Monokai style have been changed, which causes contrast degradation. The changes include:

- Error color changed from "#ed007e bg:#1e0010" to "#960050 bg:#1e0010"
- Comment color changed from "#959077" to "#75715e"
- Keyword.Namespace color changed from "#ff4689" to "#f92672"
- Operator color changed from "#ff4689" to "#f92672"
- Name.Tag color changed from "#ff4689" to "#f92672"
- Generic.Deleted color changed from "#ff4689" to "#f92672"
- Generic.Prompt color changed from "bold #ff4689" to "bold #f92672"
- Generic.Subheading color changed from "#959077" to "#75715e"

These changes result in lower contrast ratios against the background, making text harder to read for some users. This is particularly problematic for accessibility compliance.

I can reproduce this by comparing the contrast values before and after the changes:

```python
from pygments.styles import get_style_by_name
from wcag_contrast_ratio import contrast

style = get_style_by_name('monokai')
bg_color = '#272822'  # Monokai background

# Example with Comment token
comment_color = '#75715e'  # New color
old_comment_color = '#959077'  # Old color

print(f"New contrast: {contrast(comment_color, bg_color)}")
print(f"Old contrast: {contrast(old_comment_color, bg_color)}")
```

I suggest reverting these color changes to maintain the previous contrast levels. I'm happy to open a PR for this.
